feature: Sealed tests that can pass, written against the public API
description: The test writer sees the public signatures of every file the ADR names. Generations with a placeholder that cannot pass are refused. Red can be proved at an earlier ancestor commit. A sealed test file is replaced only through `hexa spec tests --replace`, with a recorded reason.

specs.description: A pub function keeps its signature and loses its body
specs.given: a Rust source containing `pub fn add(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 { let s = a + b; s }`
specs.then: the result contains `pub fn add(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 { … }` and does not contain `let s = a + b`

specs.description: Pub structs, enums, traits and impl blocks are kept, and method bodies are elided
specs.given: a source with `pub struct Store { pub path: String }`, `pub enum Mode { A, B }`, `pub trait Port { fn get(&self) -> u8; }` and `impl Store { pub fn new(path: String) -> Self { Store { path } } }`
specs.then: the result contains `pub struct Store`, `pub enum Mode`, `pub trait Port`, `impl Store` and `pub fn new(path: String) -> Self { … }`, and does not contain `Store { path }`

specs.description: Private items and mod tests are removed
specs.given: a source with `pub fn visible() {}`, `fn hidden_helper() {}`, `struct HiddenType;` and `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { #[test] fn secret_test() {} }`
specs.then: the result contains `visible` and contains none of `hidden_helper`, `HiddenType`, `mod tests` or `secret_test`

specs.description: hexa spec tests shows the writer the public signatures of each other named .rs file
specs.given: an ADR that names a port file, a domain file and `hexa-exec/src/usecase.rs` in backquotes, where usecase.rs has a pub constructor `pub fn new(store: S) -> Self` whose body holds the marker `BODY_MARKER_7`
specs.when: hexa spec tests builds the writer's inputs for that ADR
specs.then: the inputs hold the ADR text, the port and domain files whole, and the public signatures of usecase.rs including `pub fn new(store: S) -> Self { … }`

specs.description: The writer never sees the body of a non-port, non-domain file
specs.given: the same ADR, where usecase.rs's function body holds `BODY_MARKER_7`
specs.when: hexa spec tests builds the writer's inputs
specs.then: `BODY_MARKER_7` appears nowhere in the writer's inputs

specs.description: hexa spec draft does not gain the extra files
specs.given: the same ADR that names usecase.rs
specs.when: hexa spec draft builds the spec author's inputs
specs.then: the inputs hold the ADR and the port and domain files only, with no signatures or text from usecase.rs

specs.description: No function body and no private item survives, and the operation is idempotent
specs.given: any Rust source whose function bodies each contain a distinct marker string, and whose private items have distinct names
specs.when: public_signatures is called on it, and called again on its own output
specs.then: no body marker and no private item name appears in the output, and the second call returns the first call's output unchanged

specs.description: todo! and unimplemented! are reported with their 1-based lines
specs.given: a test source whose line 3 holds `todo!()` and whose line 7 holds `unimplemented!("x")`, each inside a function body
specs.then: it returns a site at line 3 whose text contains `todo!(` and a site at line 7 whose text contains `unimplemented!(`

specs.description: A panic! that is the first statement of a function or closure body is a site
specs.given: a test source with `fn make() -> Svc {` on line 1 and `panic!("stub")` on line 2 as its first statement, and a closure `let f = || { panic!("stub") };` on line 5
specs.then: sites are returned for line 2 and line 5, each with text containing `panic!(`

specs.description: A panic! inside unwrap_or_else, a match arm or an assertion message is not a site
specs.given: a test source whose only panics are `x.unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{e}"))`, a match arm `Err(e) => panic!("{e}"),` and `assert!(ok, "{}", panic_msg)`, with real code before each one in its function
specs.then: it returns no sites

specs.description: hexa spec tests refuses a generation with an unpassable site and names each site
specs.given: a generated test file that covers every scenario and holds `todo!()` at line 12 inside a helper
specs.when: hexa spec tests evaluates the generation
specs.then: the generation is refused with a message naming line 12 and `todo!(`, and no seal and no red commit is recorded

specs.description: A clean generated file has no sites and is not refused for this reason
specs.given: a generated test file with assertions only and no todo!, unimplemented! or leading panic!
specs.then: it returns an empty list

specs.description: Every todo! and unimplemented! is reported at its own line, and lines shift with inserted text
specs.given: any test source with todo!( or unimplemented!( calls placed inside function bodies at known lines
specs.when: unpassable_sites is called on it, and again after k blank lines are prepended
specs.then: the first call reports exactly one site per call, at its line, and every reported line is between 1 and the file's line count; the second call reports the same sites with each line increased by k

specs.description: Red is proved at an ancestor commit and recorded
specs.given: an ADR whose implementation exists at HEAD, and an ancestor commit C that predates the implementation
specs.when: `hexa spec tests <ADR> --red-at C` runs and every generated test fails in a worktree at C with the file added
specs.then: refs/hexa/red/<ADR> points to a commit whose tree is C's tree plus the test file, the spec's red names that commit, and the test file is committed onto HEAD

specs.description: verify --prove checks red at the recorded commit
specs.given: a spec whose red was recorded by --red-at
specs.then: the red check runs at the commit under refs/hexa/red/<ADR> and passes when the tests fail there

specs.description: A commit that is not an ancestor of HEAD is refused
specs.given: a commit D on a branch not reachable from HEAD
specs.then: it is refused for not being an ancestor of HEAD, and no ref, no red value and no commit on HEAD is written

specs.description: A test that passes at the red commit is refused
specs.given: an ancestor commit C at which one generated test already passes
specs.then: the generation is refused, naming the test that passed, and refs/hexa/red/<ADR>, the spec's red and HEAD are unchanged

specs.description: A sealed file is replaced in one commit that names the file and the reason
specs.given: a spec with a sealed test file tests/a.rs and an accepted record, and an ancestor commit C that predates the code
specs.when: `hexa spec tests <ADR> --replace --red-at C --because "helper stubbed constructor"` runs and the new generation passes the §2 and §3 checks
specs.then: exactly one new commit removes the old file and adds the new one, its message names tests/a.rs and the text `helper stubbed constructor`, the seal holds the new file's hash, and the spec's accepted record and accepted_content are unchanged

specs.description: --replace without --because is refused
specs.given: a spec with a sealed test file
specs.when: `hexa spec tests <ADR> --replace --red-at C` runs with no --because
specs.then: it is refused for the missing reason, and the sealed file, the seal and HEAD are unchanged

specs.description: A replacement that fails §2 or §3 leaves the sealed file in place
specs.given: a spec with a sealed test file, and a regeneration that holds an `unimplemented!(` site
specs.then: it is refused, naming the site, and the original sealed file and its seal hash are unchanged and no commit is made

specs.description: Editing a sealed file by hand does not count as a replacement
specs.given: a sealed test file edited by hand and committed outside the verb
specs.then: it fails, reporting that the file's hash no longer matches its seal
